parsed_output.analysis:
The specification describes a sub-machine (CollisionAvoidanceSystem) with three orthogonal (concurrent) regions, each corresponding to a type of collision avoidance (frontend, rear-end, pedestrian), which activate concurrently. The model instead defines three separate, independent states (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) as sibling substates without any orthogonal/concurrent region separator (the "--" notation in PlantUML used to denote orthogonal regions). This means the model represents them as mutually exclusive states (a normal composite state with only one active substate at a time) rather than as three concurrently active orthogonal regions, contradicting requirement 3, which explicitly requires concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls.

Additionally, entering the CollisionAvoidanceSystem state, as modeled, will only activate one of the three regions (since PlantUML defaults to a single initial transition target unless explicit "--" region separators are given), so simultaneous activation of Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian is not represented. This does not satisfy "three regions" being orthogonal, only three sequential/exclusive composite states are shown.

Also concerning requirement 2, the specification states that the sub-machine becomes active upon detecting any of the three collision types, but the model has a single unconditioned entry transition from [*] to CollisionAvoidanceSystem, without any explicit differentiation of the entry conditions (frontend collision detected, rear-end collision detected, pedestrian collision detected). This is a minor style issue but could be seen as an omission relative to the specification, since the "Collision Detected" trigger inside each region does not explicitly map back to the top-level activation trigger described in requirement 2.

Finally, exit transition "CollisionAvoidanceSystem --> [*] : Collision Avoided" implies that a single "Collision Avoided" event ends the overall sub-machine, but internally each region uses "Collision Avoided" to return from Clamping to Idle (not to exit the entire system). This creates ambiguity/inconsistency: the same event name is used both to transition within the region (back to idle) and to exit the entire composite state, which may cause non-determinism or incorrect behavios, but this: it seems like reasonable design ambiguity rather than a strict non-conformance. I'll include as a possible issue too.
</analysis>
<issues>
<issue>
<where>Overall structure of CollisionAvoidanceSystem (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian sub-states)</where>
<issue>The three regions (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) are modeled as ordinary, mutually exclusive composite sub-states rather than as orthogonal (concurrent) regions. PlantUML requires explicit "--" separators between regions to denote orthogonal/concurrent regions; without them, only one of the three sub-states can be active at any time.</issue>
<reason>Specification item 3 explicitly states that the orthogonal regions of CollisionAvoidanceSystem must allow concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls (frontend, rear-end, pedestrian) simultaneously. As modeled, the state machine cannot have more than one of these active at once, directly violating the concurrency requirement.</reason>
</issue>
<issue>
<where>Top-level entry transition: "[*] --> CollisionAvoidanceSystem"</where>
<issue>The transition into CollisionAvoidanceSystem has no guard/trigger label distinguishing which of the three collision conditions (frontend, rear-end, pedestrian) causes activation.</issue>
<reason>Specification item 2 states the sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision, or pedestrian collision is detected. The model does not capture this triggering condition on the entry transition, leaving the activation condition implicit and disconnected from the specific collision type triggers used inside each region ("Collision Detected").</reason>
</issue>
<issue>
<where>Exit transition: "CollisionAvoidanceSystem --> [*] : Collision Avoided"</where>
<issue>The same event name "Collision Avoided" is used both as an internal transition (Clamping --> Idle) within each region and as the trigger to exit the entire CollisionAvoidanceSystem state. This creates ambiguity about whether "Collision Avoided" should return the region to idle or terminate the whole system.</issue>
<reason>The specification does not describe an explicit termination condition for the composite state, and reusing the same event name for two different semantic purposes (internal recovery vs. total system exit) is inconsistent with the intended behavior of independent, concurrently operating regions each handling their own collision-avoidance cycle.</reason>
</issue>
</issues>

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
